# Caption — Portree / Isle of Skye carousel
# Status: APPROVED by Kelly 2026-10-25 · POSTED to @gfgoneglobal 2026-10-25
# Written by Moose. Do not edit the status line — only Kelly approves, only Moose updates status.

I ate this dessert on the Isle of Skye — with celiac disease. Nobody was more surprised than me.

Portree is a harbour town of about 2,500 people, so I arrived with the usual celiac expectations (low) and a bag of emergency snacks (large). Then I tested 11 restaurants — and three scored 5/5 on my GF safety scale. Swipe through the evidence:

→ The View Restaurant at Cuillin Hills Hotel — almost everything on the menu can be made GF, and the staff genuinely get celiac. 5/5. Book ahead in summer; learn from my mistakes.
→ The Quiraing — a 7 km circular walk through the most dramatic landscape I've seen in Scotland. Layers and waterproofs, always. I learned this the damp way.
→ Portree Harbour — the coloured houses everyone photographs. Yes, the pink one really is that pink.
→ The Fairy Pools — about 2.5 km round trip. Go before 10am, before the crowds and the midges. The midges do not care about your feelings.
→ Chargrill at Marmalade Hotel — GF bread starters, steak and seafood, one of my favourite meals on Skye.
→ Where to stay: Cuillin Hills Hotel — because The View is its restaurant. The best GF dinner on the island is downstairs from your room, which is exactly my kind of commute. Booking link is in the guide.

Also in the full guide: Antlers Bar & Grill (dedicated GF fryer — proper GF fish & chips), Dulse & Brose, and the rest of the 11, each with its GF score and my honest notes.

The full Portree guide — every restaurant, GF score, and map — is on the site (link in bio). The emergency snacks, mercifully, came home unopened.

Tell me your most tragic celiac travel dinner — mine involved a plain baked potato and I think about it more than I should.
